title: ATP Yield Calculator
description: Interactive calculator that shows how glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, and the citric acid cycle contribute to total ATP yield under different NADH/FADH2 conversion assumptions.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Biology
Cellular Respiration
Bioenergetics

educational.topic: ATP yield across cellular respiration stages
learningObjectives: Calculate ATP contributions from glycolysis, pyruvate oxidation, and the citric acid cycle using adjustable conversion factors.
Compare modern (~32 ATP) and classic (~38 ATP) estimates and justify the difference.
Interpret proportional graphics to explain why the citric acid cycle contributes the most ATP despite only two substrate-level ATP.
prerequisites: Understands the stages of cellular respiration
Can distinguish substrate-level vs. oxidative phosphorylation
assessmentOpportunities: Exit ticket describing how slider changes affect the ATP total
Student explanation for why modern estimates are lower

keyQuestions: Which stage’s contribution shifts the most when NADH yield changes?
Why does the modern estimate accept fewer ATP per NADH/FADH2?
commonMisconceptions: All textbooks still agree on 38 ATP per glucose.
Most ATP is produced during glycolysis.
